title: Path-Specific Counterfactual Fairness for Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Existing recommender systems may capture undesirable correlations between sensitive features and observed user behaviors, producing biased recommendations.

gap.claim: Methods that completely block sensitive-feature influences can remove fair influences that support user interests, recommendation quality, and necessary diversity.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a path-specific fair recommender system, PSF-RS, that distinguishes fair and unfair correlations involving sensitive features.
It defines path-specific bias using path-specific counterfactual inference and represents fair and unfair correlations with two latent proxy mediators.
It provides PSF-VAE, a weakly supervised variational-inference implementation for inferring latent mediators and learning a fair recommender through constrained optimization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on semi-simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of PSF-RS.
The authors report that PSF-VAE can mitigate unfairness while maximally preserving necessary recommendation diversities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems are widely used and are expected to provide personalized content without demographic discrimination.
Undesirable sensitive-feature correlations can bias recommendations, while blocking all sensitive-feature influence can reduce quality and diversity.
PSF-RS models fair and unfair correlations with latent proxy mediators and addresses path-specific bias through minimal counterfactual transformation and constrained optimization.
PSF-VAE uses weakly supervised variational inference to infer latent mediators while mitigating unfairness and preserving recommendation diversity.
Experiments on semi-simulated and real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate PSF-RS effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Sensitive features can have both fair and unfair effects on recommendation outcomes.

interpretation.claim: Fairness interventions may need to distinguish causal pathways instead of removing every influence associated with a sensitive feature.

application.claim: In recommender-system debiasing, model separate pathways or mediators and constrain only the pathways judged unfair.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the fair and unfair pathways are identified or whether this distinction transfers reliably beyond the reported datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail the constrained optimization objective or the weak-supervision procedure.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
